 Withholding Tax in Poland
 2026.11.03 
 Author: Robert Nogacki 
 Withholding tax (podatek u źródła, WHT) is a flat-rate income tax collected by the payer, known as the withholding agent, when certain amounts are paid out. It mainly concerns dividends, interest, royalties and fees for intangible services paid to non-residents. In some cases, for example domestic dividends, it is also collected on payments to Polish residents. The rules are in Articles 21 and 22 of the Corporate Income Tax Act of 15 February 1992 (the CIT Act) and Articles 29 and 30a of the Personal Income Tax Act of 26 July 1991 (the PIT Act).
 Table of Contents
 Key points 
 Scope and rates 
 Exemptions and double tax treaties 
 Due diligence and the beneficial owner 
 Pay and refund, the statement and the opinion 
 Agent duties and liability 
 What to check before every payment abroad 
 Counterparts in other jurisdictions 
 Frequently asked questions 
 Related entries 
 Withholding Tax – Further Reading 
 For CIT purposes the statutory rates are 19 percent on dividends, 20 percent on interest, royalties and intangible services, and 10 percent on specified transport income. Double tax treaties and the exemptions implementing EU directives allow the rate to be reduced or no tax to be withheld. The agent must verify the conditions with due diligence.
 Since 2022, for dividends, interest and royalties paid to related non-residents above PLN 2,000,000 a year, the pay and refund mechanism applies. Tax is withheld at the statutory rate and refunded on application, unless the agent has filed a WH-OSC statement or obtained an opinion on the application of preferences. The weight of the whole system rests on the agent, who is liable with all its assets for tax not withheld.
 Key points 
 Scope and CIT rates: dividends and other income from participation in the profits of legal persons 19 percent (Article 22(1)); interest, royalties, know-how, the use of industrial equipment and advisory, accounting, legal, advertising, management, recruitment, guarantee and similar services 20 percent (Article 21(1)(1) and (2a)); freight and passenger charges of foreign shipping and aviation enterprises 10 percent (Article 21(1)(3) and (4)). In PIT the basis is Article 29(1) (20 percent) and Article 30a(1) (19 percent).
 Reliefs: the treaty rate, or an exemption for EU and EEA companies holding at least 10 percent (dividends, Article 22(4)) or 25 percent (interest and royalties, Article 21(3)) for an uninterrupted period of 2 years. A certificate of residence is required, and for the exemptions also the taxpayer’s statement (Article 26(1), (1c) and (1f)).
 Due diligence: the agent verifies the conditions for relief taking into account the nature and scale of its activity and its links with the taxpayer (Article 26(1)). The standard is set by the Minister of Finance’s tax explanations of 3 July 2025 on the beneficial owner clause.
 Pay and refund: where the total of dividends, interest and royalties paid in the agent’s tax year to the same related non-resident exceeds PLN 2,000,000, tax is withheld on the excess at the statutory rate (Article 26(2e)). A refund follows on application (Article 28b). Withholding may be avoided by the WH-OSC statement (Article 26(7a)) or an opinion on the application of preferences (Article 26b).
 Formalities: withholding on the day of payment, remittance by the 7th day of the following month, the CIT-10Z return by the end of the first month after the year (Article 26a), IFT-2R information by the end of the third month after the year (Article 26(3a)), IFT-2 at the taxpayer’s request within 14 days (Article 26(3b)). In PIT, PIT-8AR and IFT-1R.
 Liability: the agent is liable with all its assets for tax not withheld or withheld in too low an amount (Article 30 § 1 and § 3 of the Tax Ordinance ). The taxpayer’s fault may exclude that liability (Article 30 § 5), but not between related parties (Article 30 § 5a).

 The catalogue of intangible services is open-ended through the phrase “services of a similar nature”, which generates most disputes. The case law treats as similar those services in which the elements characteristic of the listed services predominate. The name of a service in a contract does not decide the tax. What matters is the actual scope of the service, the rights to the infrastructure and the applicable treaty.
 Hosting is a good example. It is usually not a service similar to those listed in Article 21(1)(2a). The authorities nevertheless try to classify some cloud models as the use of industrial equipment under Article 21(1)(1), a notion they extend to almost any hired equipment. Comparable disputes concern commercial intermediation and insurance.
 A separate rule applies to payments connected with a non-resident’s Polish permanent establishment. The agent may refrain from withholding on payments covered by Article 21(1) if it holds the recipient’s certificate of residence and its written statement that the payments are connected with the activity of the establishment in Poland (Article 26(1d) and (1e)). The mere existence of an establishment is not enough.
 Exemptions and double tax treaties 
 Two exemptions implement EU directives. Dividends paid to an EU or EEA company that directly holds at least 10 percent of the shares for an uninterrupted period of 2 years and does not benefit from an exemption of all its income are tax-free (Article 22(4) to (4d)). The two-year condition may be met after the payment (Article 22(4b)). Interest and royalties paid to an associated EU or EEA company with a holding of at least 25 percent for 2 years are exempt if the recipient is their beneficial owner (Article 21(3) to (9)).
 The “no exemption” condition was disputed. The Minister of Finance clarified it in two general rulings: No. DD9.8202.1.2024 of 15 November 2024 for the dividend exemption under Article 22(4), and No. DD9.8202.2.2024 of 20 November 2024 for interest and royalties under Article 21(3). In both the condition refers to an entity-level exemption of the recipient from tax on all its income, not to the actual payment of tax on the specific amount. Details are in the entry on the participation exemption and in our article on the anti-abuse clause and the parent-subsidiary dividend exemption . The separate regime for Polish holding companies is described in the entry on the holding exemption .
 Double tax treaties reduce the rates for dividends, interest and royalties. They usually treat intangible services as business profits taxable in the state of residence, unless the recipient has a Polish permanent establishment. International transport has its own treaty article. Applying a treaty requires a certificate of residence (Article 26(1)) and, for passive payments, beneficial owner status. Following the Multilateral Instrument, most Polish treaties contain the principal purpose test. The map of treaties is in the entry on double taxation agreements , and the document conditioning their application in the entry on the tax residency certificate .
 Due diligence and the beneficial owner 
 Since 1 January 2019 an agent applying a treaty rate or an exemption must exercise due diligence in verifying the conditions. The standard depends on the nature and scale of the agent’s activity and on its links with the taxpayer (Article 26(1)). The beneficial owner is an entity that receives the payment for its own benefit, is not an intermediary or trustee, and carries on genuine economic activity in its state of tax residence, where the payment is connected with that activity (Article 4a(29)).
 The tax explanations of 3 July 2025 clarified the approach. The beneficial owner clause applies to passive payments, that is dividends, interest and royalties. For intangible services the agent does not examine that condition. For payments to related parties a certificate and a statement are not enough; the agent must check the recipient’s contracts and financial statements. For payments to unrelated parties a certificate of residence and the taxpayer’s statement suffice. The required substance depends on the type of activity: less is expected of a holding company than of an operating company, but the decision-makers must be real and paid by that company.
 The dividend exemption in Article 22(4) does not expressly mention beneficial owner status. The Minister of Finance nevertheless takes the view that the agent should examine it for dividends as well, deriving this from the purpose of the directive and the case law of the Court of Justice. That is an interpretative position, not the wording of the statute. At the same time the explanations allow a presumption that the condition is met where the profit distribution is taxed at least once in the EU or EEA. The practical consequences are described in our articles on beneficial ownership and dividend distributions and on withholding tax agent obligations .
 The look-through approach
 The explanations confirmed that the agent may apply the look-through approach (LTA). It allows the relief appropriate to the beneficial owner standing behind an intermediary. Before the payment the agent should establish four things: who the beneficial owner is, whether that owner recognises taxable revenue from the payment in its own state, whether the payments along the chain are of the same kind, and whether the conditions of the specific relief are met. Interest must therefore reach the owner as interest, not as a dividend. Directive-based exemptions and treaty relief are assessed separately.
 LTA is an option for the agent, not a duty of the authority. The protection offered by the explanations works only if the agent names in its forms the entity whose status is the basis for the relief. The Director of National Tax Information confirmed the admissibility of LTA for interest in a ruling of 8 September 2026 (No. 0114-KDIP2-1.4010.341.2026.1.EG). Disputes about the statutory basis of the concept still reach the administrative courts, so the risk has to be assessed for the particular chain of payments.
 The Court of Justice, in its judgments of 26 February 2019 in the Danish cases ( C-115/16, C-118/16, C-119/16 and C-299/16 , and C-116/16 and C-117/16 ), confirmed that a state may refuse an exemption to a conduit company without substance even without a domestic anti-abuse clause.
 Before an agent applies LTA or an exemption to a larger intra-group payment, it should have a written analysis of the payment chain and of the recipient’s substance. The same analysis is the basis for an application for an opinion on the application of preferences. We prepare both as part of our withholding tax advisory .
 Pay and refund, the statement and the opinion 
 The mechanism covers dividends, interest and royalties paid to the same taxpayer that is a related entity and not a Polish resident. Where their total in the agent’s tax year exceeds PLN 2,000,000, the agent withholds tax on the excess at the statutory rate, without exemptions or treaties (Article 26(2e)). For a tax year other than 12 months the threshold is calculated proportionally (Article 26(2j)). Intangible services and payments to unrelated entities remain outside the mechanism.
 Not every payment in the catalogue enters the mechanism. The Minister of Finance’s regulation of 28 December 2022 (consolidated text, Journal of Laws 2025, item 659) excludes from it, among other things, interest on Treasury bonds and payments for the use of industrial equipment, including means of transport, where the recipient is resident in a state with which Poland exchanges tax information. A separate exclusion, extended year by year, covers payments on securities held in accounts kept by technical agents (Article 26(2c)). Exclusion from the mechanism does not waive the conditions of the relief itself.
 The agent may refrain from withholding if it files a statement that it holds the documents required for the relief and, after verification with due diligence, has no knowledge justifying the supposition that the conditions are not met (Article 26(7a)). The WH-OSC statement is signed by the head of the entity or, where the entity is managed by a multi-member body, by a designated member of that body. An authorised representative may not sign it (Article 26(7b)). The deadline is the last day of the second month following the month in which the threshold was exceeded. The statement remains valid until the end of the agent’s tax year, and a follow-up statement is filed by the end of the month after the year (Article 26(7c) to (7g)). A statement filed before the threshold is exceeded is treated by the authorities as ineffective.
 The alternative is an opinion on the application of preferences. It is issued by the head of the tax office on the application of the taxpayer or the agent, as a rule within 6 months, for a fee of PLN 2,000 (Article 26b). The opinion is valid for 36 months but expires earlier if the circumstances relevant to the relief change. It is refused, among other cases, where there is a reasonable supposition that the structure is artificial.
 Tax withheld under the mechanism is refunded on application. The taxpayer applies on Form WH-WCZ. The agent may apply on Form WH-WCP if it paid the tax from its own funds and bore its economic burden (Article 28b(2)). In PIT the equivalents are WH-WPZ and WH-WPP. The refund is made without undue delay and no later than 6 months after the application is received, but the authority may extend that period where verification requires further findings (Article 28b(6) and (7)). In the proceedings the authority examines the beneficial owner and the recipient’s substance. The Ministry of Finance publishes the forms on its withholding tax pages .
 Agent duties and liability 
 The agent withholds the tax on the day of payment and remits it by the 7th day of the following month (Article 26(3)). After the year it files the CIT-10Z return by the end of the first month of the following year (Article 26a) and IFT-2R information by the end of the third month (Article 26(3a)). At the taxpayer’s request it issues IFT-2 within 14 days (Article 26(3b)). Information is filed also where no tax was withheld because of an exemption or a treaty. The competent office is the tax office specialising in non-residents. In PIT the agent accounts for the tax in PIT-8AR and IFT-1R, and the rules on certificates are the same as in CIT (Article 41(9a) to (9e) of the PIT Act).
 The agent is liable with all its assets for tax not withheld or withheld in an amount lower than due (Article 30 § 1 and § 3 of the Tax Ordinance). The authority rules on this by a decision open to appeal. Liability is excluded where the tax was not withheld through the taxpayer’s fault (Article 30 § 5), for example because of a false certificate. That exclusion does not apply, however, where the agent and the taxpayer are related parties, where they are linked by control within the meaning of the controlled foreign company rules, or where one of them is resident in a tax haven or in a state without exchange of information (Article 30 § 5a). For intra-group payments the agent is therefore liable regardless of the recipient’s fault. The rules on certificates without a validity period and on the agent’s knowledge of a change of residence (Article 26(1i) to (1l)) are assessed separately.
 Failure to withhold, or withholding too little, may be a fiscal offence under Article 78 § 1 of the Fiscal Penal Code, and failure to remit tax withheld an act under Article 77. The company’s tax liability as agent and the criminal liability of a specific individual are two different things. The second requires proof of the elements of the offence and of fault. See the entry on fiscal penal cases in Poland . A contractual shift of the tax burden to the agent (a gross-up clause) changes neither the taxpayer nor the rate. It changes only the base, because the grossed-up amount is higher. The agent’s liability becomes time-barred under the general rules described in the entry on the statute of limitations for tax obligations .
 Disputes over agent liability usually start with an audit of one larger payment. They are won with documentation gathered before the payment, not after it. In refund proceedings and liability disputes we therefore begin by reconstructing with the client what the agent knew on the day of payment.
 What to check before every payment abroad 
 The classification of the payment: whether it falls within Article 21(1) or 22(1) of the CIT Act (Article 29 or 30a of the PIT Act). A service “of a similar nature” requires an analysis of the dominant elements. For a non-resident’s Polish permanent establishment the certificate and statement under Article 26(1d) are needed.
 The recipient’s residence: a certificate covering the payment date, an original or a copy raising no doubt, 12 months’ validity where no period is stated.
 The treaty: the rate for this category, the beneficial owner clause, the principal purpose test after the MLI, the exclusive right of the state of residence for services without a permanent establishment.
 The beneficial owner and substance: due diligence documentation under the explanations of 3 July 2025, a higher standard for related parties, an assessment of the risk of the look-through approach.
 The PLN 2,000,000 threshold: aggregation of dividends, interest and royalties to the same related non-resident in the agent’s year, the regulatory exclusions, the choice between withholding and refund, the WH-OSC statement and an opinion on the application of preferences.
 Formalities: withholding on the payment date, remittance by the 7th day, CIT-10Z by the end of the first month, IFT-2R by the end of the third month after the year, retention of certificates and statements until limitation expires.
 The contract with the counterparty: a gross-up clause, the duty to deliver a certificate and beneficial owner information, liability for untrue statements.
 Counterparts in other jurisdictions 
 Most states withhold tax on dividends, interest and royalties, but rarely on services. Germany withholds on dividends at 25 percent plus the solidarity surcharge (Kapitalertragsteuer), and on royalties and other remuneration of non-residents under the separate procedure of section 50a of the Einkommensteuergesetz , as a rule at 15 percent. Treaty relief is applied after an exemption certificate from the Federal Central Tax Office or by way of refund. The United States applies a 30 percent rate reduced by treaties on the basis of Forms W-8BEN, with its own FATCA regime. Poland stands out for the broad catalogue of intangible services subject to withholding and for the pay and refund mechanism with a statement by the head of the entity made under fiscal penal liability.
 Frequently asked questions 
 What is withholding tax in Poland?
 A flat-rate income tax collected by the payer on certain amounts, mainly those paid to non-residents and in some cases also to residents. For CIT purposes the rates are 19 percent on dividends, 20 percent on interest, royalties and intangible services, and 10 percent on specified transport income (Articles 21 and 22 of the CIT Act). In PIT the basis is Articles 29 and 30a of the PIT Act.
 When can withholding tax not be collected?
 Where a double tax treaty allocates the taxing right to the recipient’s state of residence, or where the conditions of the exemption for EU and EEA companies are met (Articles 21(3) and 22(4) of the CIT Act). In both cases the agent needs a certificate of residence and must exercise due diligence, and for the exemptions must obtain the taxpayer’s statement.
 How does the pay and refund mechanism work?
 For dividends, interest and royalties paid to a related non-resident above PLN 2,000,000 a year, the agent withholds tax on the excess at the statutory rate. A refund follows on application, as a rule within 6 months (Articles 26(2e) and 28b). Withholding can be avoided by a WH-OSC statement or an opinion on the application of preferences, but the conditions of the relief must be met regardless of those documents.
 Who is the beneficial owner?
 An entity that receives the payment for its own benefit, decides on its use, bears the economic risk, is not an intermediary or trustee and carries on genuine activity in its state of tax residence (Article 4a(29) of the CIT Act). The explanations of 3 July 2025 set out how the agent is to examine this.
 Are intangible services from foreign companies subject to Polish withholding tax?
 Yes, under the statute at 20 percent on advisory, accounting, legal, advertising, management, data processing, recruitment, guarantee and similar services (Article 21(1)(2a) of the CIT Act). With a certificate of residence most treaties allow no withholding, because they treat such fees as business profits.
 Who is liable for withholding tax that was not collected?
 The agent, with all its assets (Article 30 of the Tax Ordinance). The taxpayer’s fault may exclude that liability, but not where the agent and the taxpayer are related parties (Article 30 § 5a). Failure to withhold may also be a fiscal offence under Article 78 of the Fiscal Penal Code.

 Robert Nogacki Robert Nogacki is a Polish attorney at law (radca prawny), the founder and managing partner of Kancelaria Prawna Skarbiec (Skarbiec Law Firm), which has operated continuously since 2006.
 The law is equal for everyone, but the parties rarely are: on one side stands an organization with time, money, and lawyers, on the other a person with one business, one nest egg, and one life.
 Clients rarely come to him with a legal problem. They come with a problem that also has a legal side: an audit that began with a single invoice, money entrusted to someone who has disappeared, a company that has to be passed on before it is too late. Most such matters are decided long before the first letter is written, in decisions made without asking and in deadlines nobody remembered. So he begins by asking how the client got here, not what the client should have done.
 He advises entrepreneurs and families from more than a dozen countries, including those whose accounts the tax office has just seized and who do not know what to do tomorrow morning. He defends them in tax audits, customs and fiscal inspections, disputes with the tax authorities, and criminal tax proceedings. He represents victims of investment fraud and Ponzi schemes. He helps families set up family foundations and plan succession, so that a life’s work outlasts a single generation.
 Not every case can be won. Every case can be run so that the client knows where they stand. Since 2006 he has represented the victims in the WGI case (Warszawska Grupa Inwestycyjna, the Warsaw Investment Group), one of the longest criminal cases in the history of the Polish financial market, because some things must not be left half finished, even when they take two decades. In the case of the collapsed cryptocurrency exchange Zonda (Zondacrypto, operated by BB Trade Estonia OÜ), he represents several hundred victims in the criminal investigation conducted by Poland’s National Prosecutor’s Office and in the Estonian bankruptcy proceedings.
 Kancelaria Prawna Skarbiec is listed in the rankings of Poland’s largest tax advisory firms published by Dziennik Gazeta Prawna and Rzeczpospolita, and it is a four-time recipient (2015 to 2018) of the European Medal awarded by the Business Centre Club and the European Economic and Social Committee. Robert Nogacki publishes regularly, in the press and on the firm’s website, for people who have a problem rather than a law degree, because a legal opinion the client cannot understand protects only the lawyer.
 He believes that the best legal advice is the kind that means the client never has to appear in court.
